title: The Names of God
lead: The Hebrew Bible calls God by his personal name, YHWH (printed "the LORD"), and by titles such as Elohim (God), Adonai (Lord) and Shaddai (the Almighty). Each name says something about who God is and how he relates to his people.

sections.b: YHWH, God's personal name, is explained to Moses as "I am who I am" (Exodus 3:14–15) and appears about 6,800 times. Jewish readers say Adonai instead, and most English Bibles print "the LORD." Elohim, "God," is plural in form but used with singular verbs for Israel's God (Genesis 1:1). Adonai means "my Lord." El Shaddai, "God Almighty," is the name known to the patriarchs (Genesis 17:1; Exodus 6:3). Other titles include El Elyon, "God Most High" (Genesis 14:18–20), and YHWH Sabaoth, "the LORD of hosts" (1 Samuel 1:3; Isaiah 6:3).
